title: Immunostaining of tumor-infiltrating immune-cell-related markers and cytokines in the tumor fractional radiation model of host PD-L1-deficient mice
protocol: Cut the hair from the left and right flanks of mice to expose the skin.
Take LLC cells seeded in 10-cm dishes from the cell incubator to the biosafety cabinet.
Wash LLC cells with 1 mL PBS buffer for 1–2 times gently, then discard the buffer.
Add 1 mL trypsin to the dish and place it back into the cell incubator for 1 min.
Add 1 mL complete DMEM medium to stop digestion when cells become round under a microscope.
Collect dissociated cells into 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge at 100 g for 5 minutes, then discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS buffer and take out 100 μL cell suspension.
Count the number of cells using a cell counter.
Adjust the cell concentration to 2 × 10^7 cells/mL with PBS buffer.
Place the tube on ice immediately after adjusting concentration.
Mix the cell suspension evenly.
Inject 100 μL of the cell suspension subcutaneously into the right flank of each mouse.
Label the formed xenograft as the primary tumor.
Record this day as day 0.
Adjust the number of tumor cells inoculated according to the immune character of mice and type of tumor cell line.
Prepare LLC cells with a concentration of 2 × 10^7 cells/mL on day 3,6.
Inject 100 μL cell suspension subcutaneously into the left flank of each mouse to generate an abscopal xenograft tumor.
Record tumor volumes every two days until mice are killed.
Calculate tumor volume using V = (width² × length)/2.
Administer anti-IFNAR-1 (500 μg per mouse) into mice by intraperitoneal injection.
Ensure quick administration to maintain antibody valence and inject within 30 minutes.
Irradiate the primary tumor with a volume of about 50 mm³ with a total dose of 24 Gy X-rays in 3 fractions over 3 consecutive days (8 Gy × 3).
Gently clamp out the xenograft tumor for irradiation, shielding the rest of the mouse body with lead plates greater than 1 cm thick.
Calculate the average weight of mice administered with HCQ solution using M as the mass of each mouse and n as the number of mice requiring HCQ administration.
Record the value of average weight as \( \bar{M} = \frac{\sum_{i=0}^{n} M}{n} \) (g).
Calculate the amount of corresponding reagent based on the average weight.
Calculate the total mass of HCQ powder required using the formula m = 0.05 × n × M (mg).
Dissolve the calculated mass of HCQ powder in saline in a 5 mL EP tube.
Inject 100 μL HCQ solution or saline intraperitoneally into mice.
Irradiate mice with X-ray two hours after drug administration.
Inject 1% pentobarbital sodium intraperitoneally into mice for anesthesia at a dose of 50 mg/100 g.
Place the anesthetized mouse into a lead mold.
Gently clamp out the tumor with tweezers and shield other areas with lead plates.
Irradiate the tumor with 8 Gy X-ray.
Observe the state of mice closely after irradiation until all mice wake up.
Carry out the administration of HCQ and irradiation protocols for the next two days.
Kill the mice and strip out the transplanted tumor after 21 days of the first tumor cell injection.
Sacrifice the mice by neck breaking as quickly as possible to alleviate pain.
Pin down the mouse on its back using needles.
Spray the mouse body with 75% ethanol.
Cut the mouse skin from the area near the bottom of abdomen to neck with scissors.
Strip out the tumor capsule with a tweezer and dissect out the tumor gently.
Clean the tumor and put it into a marked 50 mL conical tube containing PBS buffer.
Weigh the tumor.
Cut the tumor into small pieces less than 1 mm.
Transfer the tumor tissues into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add RPMI medium supplemented with 2% FBS to the 50 mL conical tube at 1 mL per 1 mg of tissue.
Add an appropriate amount of collagenase IV into the 50 mL conical tube to achieve a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.
Put the conical tube into a shaking bath at 37°C until the tissue is digested.
Pass the tissue homogenate through a 70 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Clean the strainer several times with serum-free RPMI.
Add DNase to the homogenate and incubate at 37°C for 15 min if necessary.
Collect cells from the tissue homogenate after centrifugation at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend collected cells in PBS buffer.
Take a small portion of cells for counting.
Adjust cell density to 1 × 10^7 cells/mL with PBS buffer.
Add 100 μL of cell suspension to 1.5 mL EP tubes for cell surface antigen staining, containing 10^6 cells per tube.
Resuspend 2 × 10^6 cells in 500 μL RPMI medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
Add 1 μL cell stimulation cocktail (containing protein transport inhibitors) to the cell suspension for intracellular cytokine staining.
Culture cells in a 12-well plate in an incubator containing 5% CO2 at 37°C for 16 hours.
Pre-incubate with Fc receptor blocker (TruStain FcX™ PLUS) for 5–10 min on ice, using 0.25 μg/10^6 cells in 100 μL FACS buffer.
Add fluorescence-labeled antibodies to stain the cells and keep away from light.
Mix Anti-CD3 (2 μg/mL), anti-CD4 (1 μg/mL), anti-CD8 (1 μg/mL), and anti-NK1.1 (1 μg/mL) for one group of samples.
Mix Anti-CD3 (2 μg/mL), anti-CD8 (1 μg/mL), anti-CD44 (1 μg/mL), anti-CD62L (1 μg/mL), and anti-PD-1 (1 μg/mL) for another group of samples.
Add 50 μL cell suspension to each of the seven EP tubes for single staining group samples.
Add one antibody (anti-CD3, anti-CD4, anti-CD8, anti-NK1.1, anti-CD44, anti-CD62L, or anti-PD-1) to each tube at half the amount used in the experimental groups.
Keep the whole process of staining away from light to avoid loss of fluorescence.
Set each antibody with a single staining tube to adjust the fluorescence compensation.
Stain the sample at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to wash cells.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Add 400 μL FACS buffer to resuspend cells in preparation for flow cytometry analysis.
Collect the cells and centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant after 16 h of cell stimulation.
Add 500 μL FACS buffer to wash cells.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells with 100 μL FACS buffer.
Pre-incubate with Fc receptor blocker (TruStain FcX™ PLUS) for 5–10 min on ice, 0.25 μg/106 cells in 100 μL FACS buffer.
Add CD8 fluorescent antibody (1 μg/mL) to stain cells in dark condition for 30 min at 4°C.
Stain cells with antibodies of cell surface marker in advance if not sorted.
Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each tube to wash the cells, and centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Add 100 μL fixation buffer to fix the cells at 4°C for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cells with 100 μL 1× perm/wash buffer.
Add fluorescence-labeled antibody to stain cell cytokines in dark condition.
Stain the sample at 4°C for 30 min in the dark after adding the antibody.
Add 500 μL 1× perm/wash buffer to wash cells, centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min to remove the supernatant.
Add 400 μL FACS buffer into the cells for flow cytometry analysis.
Filter the single cell suspension with a 200-mesh filter membrane and place them in the flow tubes for flow cytometry analysis.
Make a pair combination according to the required staining indicators.
Set the X-Y plot on the computer in advance.
Collect cells from single staining tubes respectively.
Adjust the compensation value so that there is a detection signal on the staining channel and no signal on other non-staining channels.
Set CD3 vs CD4 gate, adjust fluorescent compensation with single staining tube of CD3.
Set CD3 vs CD8 gate, adjust fluorescent compensation with single staining tube of CD3.
Set CD4 vs CD8 gate, adjust fluorescent compensation with single staining tube of CD4 and CD8 respectively.
Analyze cell samples with a flow cytometry.
Collect 1 × 10^5 cells for samples stained only on the cell surface.
Collect 5 × 10^4 cells for cell samples detecting intracellular factors.
Set the initial FSC vs SSC gate to circle the lymphocyte population.
Set FSC-H vs FSC-W gate to remove adherent cells.
Set SSC-H vs SSC-W gate to remove adherent cells.
Set CD3 vs SSC gate to circle CD3+ T lymphocytes.
Set CD4 vs CD8 gate to circle CD4+ T lymphocytes and CD8+ T lymphocytes.
Set CD8 vs SSC gate to circle CD8+ T lymphocytes.
Set CD8 vs PD-1 gate to circle CD8+PD-1+ T lymphocytes.
Set CD62L vs CD44 gate to circle CD44+CD62L- T lymphocytes.
Set CD8 vs IFN-γ gate to circle CD8+PD-1+ T lymphocytes.
Operate under dark conditions for flow cytometric detection.
Analyze sorting results with FlowJo software.
Set the initial FSC vs SSC gate to identify T lymphocytes.
Set FSC-H vs FSC-W gate to remove adherent cells.
Set SSC-H vs SSC-W gate to further exclude non-T cell populations.
Gate CD3+ cells to identify total tumor-derived T lymphocytes.
Gating of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells within the CD3+ T cell population.
Gating of PD-1+ T cells within the CD8+ T cell population.
Gating of CD44+CD62L- T cells within the CD8+ T cell population.
Set the initial FSC vs SSC gate to identify T lymphocytes for IFN-γ analysis.
Set FSC-H vs FSC-W gate and SSC-H vs SSC-W gate to remove adherent cells for IFN-γ analysis.
Gate CD3+ cells to identify total tumor-derived T lymphocytes for IFN-γ analysis.
Gating of CD8+ T cells within the CD3+ T cell population for IFN-γ analysis.
Gating of IFN-γ+ T cells within the CD8+ T cell population for IFN-γ analysis.
Operate under dark condition during flow cytometry analysis.
